narrative.overview:
The office lives by the 26th, so the 26th is the one shape in the product. A midnight rail and band form one L-shaped field around a pale grey-blue page, and a single cantaloupe disc hangs over the edge of that field to show where the month is heading. Flat colour and confident Hebrew from the Israeli poster and stamp tradition set the tone; badges are gone, and state reads as a small flat mark.

The world is built for a clerk who keeps it open all day. Work sits in white panels with thin borders on the tinted page, because the user asked for clear separation between sections. Panels stay square and flat, with no shadows or gradients. Rank comes from size and weight. Cantaloupe is rationed so the clerk's next action is the loudest thing on any screen, and electric blue shows where the clerk is and what is selected. One form repeats at every scale, from the logo to the month band to the login poster.

Three decisions were made by the builder during review and still await the user. They are described below as built and marked **Pending user decision**: Secular One on section titles, popup titles and the countdown as well as page titles; page actions directly under the page title instead of in the title row; and outlined bars for scheduled reminders beside the white bars in the month strip.
keyCharacteristics: An L-shaped midnight field, a pale page, white bordered panels, one cantaloupe disc.
Square corners and flat colour everywhere except the WhatsApp simulator.
Electric blue for selection and place, cantaloupe for the 26th and the next action.
Secular One for titles and headline figures, Assistant for everything else, tabular figures throughout.
Hebrew right to left first, with numbers, phones and IDs kept left to right inside it.
Light and dark themes share one set of tokens, swapped at the root.

rules.name: The Two Meanings Rule
rules.body: Cantaloupe means the 26th or the clerk's next action. That covers the disc, the strip's today marker, the primary button, the review banner, the review state mark and the "requested a call" share of a campaign. The text caret and text selection are the only ambient uses.

rules.name: The One Cantaloupe Button Rule
rules.body: A view has at most one cantaloupe button. A disabled primary turns grey, so cantaloupe never sits on something that cannot be pressed.

rules.name: The Current Place Rule
rules.body: A solid electric blue fill with white text means selected or current. Step discs, avatars and the paid share of a campaign bar are the only other fills.

rules.name: The True Warning Rule
rules.body: Amber and red appear only for real warnings, failures and destructive actions, never for emphasis.

rules.name: The WhatsApp Quarantine Rule
rules.body: The `wa-*` colours, soft corners and bubble shadow exist only where the client's WhatsApp is being shown. They never leak into the dashboard, and the dashboard's rules never reshape WhatsApp.

rules.name: The Poster Voice Rule
rules.body: Secular One carries only page, section and popup titles, the countdown, headline tally figures, the disc numeral and the wordmark. Everything else is Assistant. It has one weight, so it is never bolded. Pending user decision: the original direction limited it to page titles; the build extends it to section titles, popup titles and the countdown.

rules.name: The Size and Weight Rule
rules.body: Rank comes from size and weight, with the strongest ink for the highest rank. No letter-spacing, no decorative labels above titles, no coloured headings.

rules.name: The Exact Figures Rule
rules.body: Tabular figures are on globally, and numbers, phones and IDs sit in left-to-right runs inside Hebrew text. A tax or money figure is never rounded, hidden or decorated.

rules.name: The L-Field Rule
rules.body: The rail and band are one continuous midnight field, marked only by a 10% white hairline, and every authenticated page carries the band.

rules.name: The Fixed Window Rule
rules.body: The band and Send Request keep their height budget. New band content must not push Send Request into a page scroll on laptop sizes.

rules.name: The Flat Poster Rule
rules.body: No shadows or gradients on dashboard surfaces. A surface separates by colour, by a thin border or by overlap. The WhatsApp wallpaper's dot texture and bubble shadow stay as part of the WhatsApp Quarantine Rule.

rules.name: The Square and Disc Rule
rules.body: Rectangles are square; a curve is a full circle, and the toggle is the only exception. New round forms hold a number, a person's initials or a state, and a numbered cantaloupe disc always reads 26.

dos: Do let cantaloupe mark the single next action on each view, with midnight text.
Do put working sections in white panels with a 1px border on the Pale Page.
Do show state with a State Mark and a text label, in a fixed position.
Do keep every table row on one type size and, where the column allows it, one line.
Do use the Deadline Disc whenever the 26th is named visually.
Do lay pages out with container queries against the content column.
Do check every new surface in light mode, dark mode and right-to-left, with figures left to right.
Do keep the phone simulator faithful to WhatsApp, whatever the dashboard does.
donts: Don't use coloured status pills or badges for state.
Don't add shadows, gradients or rounded rectangles to dashboard surfaces.
Don't use cantaloupe for decoration or for a second button on a view.
Don't use amber or red for emphasis without a real warning behind it.
Don't use `wa-*` tokens or WhatsApp radii outside WhatsApp views.
Don't put any number but 26 in a cantaloupe disc.
Don't use Secular One for body text, form labels, table rows or buttons.
Don't render manager-only controls as disabled or hidden elements for workers; leave them out.
